verdict.rationale: Lithic's Auth Rules v2 lets you write rules on MCC and apply them at the program, account or card level, and those rules make decisions on the card authorization stream. That covers MCC-based restriction at authorization time. The docs do not explicitly describe allowlist versus blocklist modes, and there is no evidence of a single-merchant lock; ASA is only a building block for custom decisioning and earns no credit. Missing for 10: explicit MCC allowlist/blocklist semantics, single-merchant lock capability, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can restrict where a card works — merchant category (MCC) allowlists and blocklists, and single-merchant locks — applied at authorization time

citations.quote: By defining rules based on high-signal attributes like MCC, country, currency, and risk score, you can enforce business-specific authorization logic at the program, account, or card level, without managing additional infrastructure.
the Auth Rules engine supports multiple event streams, each enabling decisioning for a different payment flow: card authorizations
Configure Authorization Rules controlling merchant categories, transaction limits, and velocity
